name: change-coupling
question: Which files and modules repeatedly change together in the same commits (co-change) across module boundaries — the language-agnostic coupling signal no import graph sees?
cost_provenance: measured 2026-07-07 on the ULDF framework repo under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment): 482 commits / ~1.6k distinct files over the 180-day window mined in ~4.8s cold; cached rerun ~0.8s. Pessimistic-honest per ORACLE-COST-01. On-demand (not in the every-session briefing fan-out), so the fast-lane 15s briefing budget does not apply; the declared budget is for the /0-uldf-oracle audit and any slow-lane consumer.

schema.reason: string (present on no-data; the honest reason the history could not be analyzed)
schema.shallow: boolean (true when the repository is a shallow clone — history may be truncated)

window.commitsAnalyzed: integer (non-merge commits actually seen in the window)
window.qualifyingCommits: integer (commits with 2..bulkCommitMax files — the ones that contribute pairs)

filters.bulkCommitMax: integer (commits touching MORE than this many files are excluded — bulk renames/format sweeps)
filters.minCoChanges: integer (a pair must co-change at least this many times to be reported)
filters.excludedCommits: integer (count of commits excluded by the bulk filter)

schema.filePairs: array of {a, b, coChanges} — file pairs co-changing >= minCoChanges, desc, capped at 50
schema.modulePairs: array of {moduleA, moduleB, coChanges, crossBoundary} — module-level aggregation, desc, capped at 50
schema.crossBoundaryTop: array of {moduleA, moduleB, coChanges, crossBoundary:true} — the boundary-crossing subset (the finding), desc, capped at 50
schema.truncated: boolean (true when any array was capped at 50 — no silent drops)
schema.cached: boolean (true when served from the HEAD+config-keyed session-state cache)
schema.briefing: string (advisory one-liner; frames results as co-change EVIDENCE, not proven dependency)

freshness.key: HEAD sha + changeCoupling config; cache at .claude/session-state/change-coupling-cache.json (session-state, never committed)

fallback: Mine co-change by hand: `git -c core.quotepath=off log --name-only --no-merges --since='180 days ago' --pretty=format:'@@%H'`, then for each commit with 2..20 files count every unordered file pair; pairs reaching 5+ co-changes across module boundaries (map each file to its nearest-ancestor-README directory) are coupled IN FACT whatever the import graph says. This is CORRELATION (co-change evidence), never proven dependency — advisory only.

provenance.note: Scrutiny ADD proposal A2 (KEEP verdict), Arc 1 deterministic detection substrate. The language-agnostic coupling leg: two files/modules that repeatedly change in the same commits are coupled in fact — and this needs only git log, so it covers config/doc/cross-language coupling no parser sees, including this repo's own bash/PowerShell/markdown substrate (the .sh<->.ps1 twin pairs surface strongly). One of the M3 'second trigger family' members: high boundary-crossing co-change is the architecture-decomposition trigger the capacity-only (>85% context) rule misses. ADVISORY, correlation-not-dependency (the A2 critic's binding condition): never blocks, never exits nonzero on findings. NO-DATA honesty: not-a-repo / no history / insufficient history / no co-change-analyzable commits -> status:no-data with a reason, never a silent empty-but-ok that reads as 'no coupling'. Rename/bulk-commit filters keep format sweeps from polluting the signal (CodeScene change-coupling lineage).

config.comment: All keys optional with these defaults. Cache is keyed by HEAD sha + these four values, so a config change invalidates the cache. bulkCommitMax excludes bulk renames/format sweeps (a k-file commit contributes O(k^2) pairs; the <=20 cap keeps it to <=190 pairs/commit). Module mapping is nearest-ancestor directory containing README.md, falling back to the top-level directory component (or '(root)') for README-less trees.
